html:
A web of jungle paths, roads and river routes that ran from North Vietnam through Laos and Cambodia to South Vietnam, carrying men and supplies for the communist side in the Vietnam War.

North Vietnam set up a special army unit to build it in 1959. At first porters walked loads south on foot and on bicycles over the Truong Son mountains. Over the years it grew into thousands of kilometres of routes able to take trucks, with fuel pipelines, repair shops, hospitals and hidden depots. Hundreds of thousands of soldiers marched down it to fight for the Viet Cong.

The United States tried for years to cut it. It dropped huge tonnages of bombs on Laos, sprayed defoliants on the forest, and scattered sensors to track trucks. Losses were heavy, but the flow never stopped. Laos became, by weight of bombs per person, the most bombed country in history, and unexploded bombs still kill people there.

The trail was named after Hồ Chí Minh. It made possible the final offensive that ended with the fall of Saigon in 1975.
sum: A web of jungle paths, roads and river routes that ran from North Vietnam through Laos and Cambodia to South Vietnam, carrying men and supplies for the communist side in the Vietnam War.
